## How this file works

1. The block between the `---` lines is the **header** (YAML). It sets title, author, and output format.
2. Text is written in Markdown.
3. Code lives in **chunks**. Quarto runs each chunk and puts the output in the report.

Click **Render** in RStudio. The report opens as an HTML file.

## A chunk with a graph

```{r}
#| label: graph
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Flipper length and body mass of 344 penguins."
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, palmerpenguins)

penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Penguins with longer flippers weigh more",
       x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Body mass (g)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Chunk options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `#| echo: false` | Show the graph, hide the code |
| `#| eval: false` | Show the code, do not run it |
| `#| warning: false` | Hide warnings |
| `#| fig-cap: "..."` | Add a figure caption |

## Other formats

Change `format:` in the header and render again:

- `html`: web page
- `pdf`: PDF (needs a LaTeX installation: run `quarto install tinytex`)
- `docx`: Word file
- `gfm`: Markdown for GitHub
